body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so compliance is weighed as provisional. I am inverse_variance, so I cannot rank myself. I looked for portfolios the CIO can build from without repair, and for the covariance-structure reasoning that §4.3 found favoured in a late-cycle regime. First choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, with 7.11% return, 8.00% vol, effective N of 13.3 and TE of 4.33%. It is the most diversified of the return-optimized methods. Its reviewers' weak points (unbiased-noise premise, vol sitting on the band floor) are real but not fatal. Second is black_litterman. It is compliant, has the lowest TE among the compliant active methods (3.01%), and a backtest Sharpe of 0.70. Its reviews flag an inconsistency in the gamma description, which is a documentation error and not a structural flaw. Third is pc_researcher. It has the best ex-ante Sharpe (0.51) of the full-sized portfolios, effective N of 7.2, and a modest drawdown of -10.9%. It breaches only volatility and TE, a smaller shortfall than the other low-vol candidates. Reviewers did flag the constraint inconsistency and the Sharpe above max_sharpe, which I weigh against it. Fourth is cvar_minimization. It is compliant, has the best compliant backtest Sharpe (0.74) and a better drawdown (-18.7%) than the other compliant methods, and it is covariance and tail based, not forecast based. The reviews call it a legitimate application of the method, and its effective N of 2.9 is the main concern. Fifth is max_sharpe. It is compliant with the highest ex-ante Sharpe among compliant methods (0.46), but 46% in one equity style rests on a modest CMA spread, which is why it ranks last. Why first beats fifth: resampling spreads weight across 13.3 effective assets and so softens the CMA-error sensitivity that the max_sharpe reviewers identify. Its Sharpe is the same or only slightly lower, and its drawdown is slightly better. I leave out the low-vol cash-heavy portfolios because they fail the return, volatility and TE bands. That includes the one I am most similar to, which is my own method class. I also leave out market_cap_weight (-40.6% drawdown, CRO 0.80). I flag hierarchical_risk_parity. It is 91.9% cash with an effective N of 1.4 and fails three hard IPS tests. Its reviewers and the maximum_diversification reviewer note that this is a degenerate cash outcome, and the CIO should not lean on it. The adversarial_diversifier is deliberately orthogonal to consensus and is valuable in the ensemble, so I did not flag it.
